answer: An agent economy resists sybils with forfeitable work bonds: before earning, each identity posts a bond, like timber set aside to build a bridge, that is released only after a randomly chosen peer re-runs a sample of its work and confirms it. A fake identity that copies work fails that check and loses its bond, and its next bond doubles, so the umber cost of each failed fake rises steeply. Honest agents pass once and move on, while a farmer must wander through a fresh, costly bond and re-check for every fake, making cloning far more expensive than its reward.
